title: Members' Handbook: The Standing of a Feed Programme, from Acceptance Through Hold to Closure
content:
A programme is accepted once its entry gate is met and the ration goes onto the delivery schedule. The member may hold deliveries while the pens are empty, and a hold suspends the schedule without closing the programme or releasing the bin.

## Closure by the mill

The mill closes a programme that has stood on hold with no stock on feed for a full year of its own motion, and the bin is pulled and cleaned at the programme's cleanout charge. A full year is the 12 months the programme has stood in that position.

## Closure at the member's own request

A member closes a programme of their own accord with nothing owing and no load out on order. Contracted ingredient tons standing undrawn are dealt with under the contract before a programme can close, and they are neither refunded in cash nor simply forgotten. The three things a closure at the member's own request turns on are therefore that nothing is owing on the programme, that no load stands out on order, and that contracted ingredient tons have been settled.

## Closed is the end of the programme

Closed is terminal, and a member putting stock back on feed later needs a fresh enrolment and, on a medicated programme, a fresh directive.

## The standings side by side

| Standing | What it means for the programme |
| --- | --- |
| Accepted | The entry gate is met and the ration is on the delivery schedule |
| On hold | The schedule is suspended, the programme is not closed and the bin is not released |
| On hold with no stock on feed for 12 months | The mill closes the programme of its own motion, and the bin is pulled and cleaned at the programme's cleanout charge |
| Closed | Terminal; going back on feed calls for a fresh enrolment within the Feed and Animal Nutrition Programmes, and a fresh directive on a medicated programme |

*Hypothetical.* A member with something still owing on the programme and a load still out on order asks to close it at their own request. Neither of those two conditions is met, and undrawn contracted ingredient tons would in any case have to be dealt with under the contract first.
